settings.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Tennessee Plumbing

items.item_title: Why is my faucet still dripping after I turned it off?
Can a running toilet really increase my water bill?
How long do garbage disposals usually last?
What is a frost-free hydrant and do I need one?
Should I replace my washing machine hoses?

settings.editor: A dripping faucet is usually caused by a worn-out washer, O-ring, or cartridge inside the handle. If ignored, a single leaky faucet can waste hundreds of gallons of water per year. We can typically repair these issues in a single visit with our stocked service trucks.

Yes, a running toilet is one of the most common causes of high water bills in Middle Tennessee. This is often due to a faulty flapper or fill valve that prevents the tank from sealing. Repairing this promptly can save you significant money on your monthly utility costs.

Most standard garbage disposals last between 8 and 12 years. If your disposal is frequently jamming, making loud metallic noises, or leaking from the bottom, it is likely time for a professional replacement. We install high-torque models that are less prone to clogs.

A frost-free hydrant is an outdoor faucet designed to prevent water from sitting in the "freeze zone" of your pipes. Given the freezing winter temperatures in Tennessee, these are essential for preventing burst pipes and costly water damage during the winter months.

We recommend replacing standard rubber hoses every 3–5 years or immediately if you see any "bulging". We install braided stainless steel hoses, which are far more resistant to pressure bursts, providing much-needed protection for your laundry room.
